questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) The scores of students in an examination are recorded as follows

| Score ($x$) | Frequency ($f$) |
|---|---|
| 8 - 12 | 6 |
| 13 - 17 | 8 |
| 18 - 22 | 12 |
| 23 - 27 | 8 |
| 28 - 32 | 6 |

State:

(a) the number of classes or intervals in the distribution
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each row of the table is one class: $8-12$, $13-17$, $18-22$, $23-27$ and $28-32$.

**Answer: $5$ classes.**

The upper class limit is the largest value written in the class $23-27$.

**Answer: $27$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) the lower and upper class boundaries of $13-17$
questions.corrige_markdown:
The classes are separated by a gap of 1 unit ($12$ then $13$), so each boundary lies half a unit beyond the limits: lower boundary $=13-0.5=12.5$ and upper boundary $=17+0.5=17.5$.

**Answer: lower class boundary $=12.5$, upper class boundary $=17.5$.**

The modal class is the class with the highest frequency. The highest frequency is $12$, for the class $18-22$.

**Answer: the modal class is $18-22$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
find:

(e) the total number of students who wrote the examination
(f) the class mark of the class $18-22$. *[10 marks for (i)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The class mark is the mid-value of the class: $\dfrac{18+22}{2}=\dfrac{40}{2}=20$.

**Answer: the class mark is $20$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) In a certain class of 40 students, where they speak both English and French,

- 18 students speak English (E) only
- 10 students speak French (F) only
- 3 do not speak neither English nor French

By drawing a Venn diagram or otherwise,

Find the number of students speaking both English and French *[5 marks for (ii)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $x$ be the number of students who speak both English and French. The Venn diagram has four regions inside the universal set of $40$ students: E only $=18$, both (E $\cap$ F) $=x$, F only $=10$, and outside both circles $=3$.

All the regions add up to $40$: $18+x+10+3=40$, so $31+x=40$ and $x=9$.

Check: $n(E)=18+9=27$, $n(F)=10+9=19$, $n(E\cup F)=18+9+10=37$ and $40-37=3$ students speak neither language.

**Answer: $9$ students speak both English and French.**
